# phase-111 — Stop dispatch from marking a phase done while its reviewer still has open MAJOR findings

## You must change `rbops/dispatch.sh`

This phase declares `must_touch: [rbops/dispatch.sh]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
AGENTS.md:258 states plainly 'A phase with open BLOCKER/MAJOR findings is not `.done`', and AGENTS.md section 5 says BLOCKER and MAJOR findings 'are then fixed by a fresh implementer run, and the full gate is run again'. rbops/dispatch.sh:912 computes `blocking` with a regex over `BLOCKER|CRITICAL` only, and rbops/dispatch.sh:923-925 then reads `elif [ "$has_sev" -gt 0 ]; then log "...findings present, none blocking - shipping"; break` - so a review whose verdict is `REVIEW VERDICT: FINDINGS 1` and whose only finding is tagged [MAJOR] exits the review loop and ships. This is not theoretical: logs/phase-080.review.3.log ends with a [MAJOR] at src/parser.rs:1813 and `REVIEW VERDICT: FINDINGS 1`, and `touch phases/phase-080/.done` ran at 06:51, the same minute. The defect it shipped is still live on main and is phase-110's finding. Marked `manual: true` for the reason phase-092/093 are: fixing this means editing rbops/dispatch.sh, which AGENTS.md hard rule 1 forbids an agent to touch, so an agent cannot land it and declaring it runnable would just burn attempts.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make dispatch treat an open MAJOR exactly as it treats an open BLOCKER - fix and re-gate - so a phase cannot reach `.done` with an unreviewed MAJOR outstanding.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-111
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] rbops/dispatch.sh:912 `blocking` counts MAJOR as well as BLOCKER and CRITICAL, so a review log tagged [MAJOR] does not reach the shipping branch at dispatch.sh:923
- [ ] a smoke check in rbops/smoke.sh feeds the reviewer parser a synthetic review log containing one [MAJOR] and asserts dispatch does NOT write .done
- [ ] a smoke check feeds it `REVIEW VERDICT: CLEAN` and asserts .done IS written, so the change did not simply block everything
- [ ] the smoke suite still passes end to end
- [ ] phases/phase-080/.done is re-opened for review, or its MAJOR is recorded as fixed by phase-110

## Constraints

- Do not touch `.github/workflows/`, `rbops/`, `.opencode/agent/`, or
  `rbops/phases.json`. The gate rejects these paths, and the bot token has no
  `workflows` scope so a push touching `.github/` is refused by GitHub.
- Do not weaken, delete or re-scope any existing test.
- Do not change the language surface listed in `phases/INVARIANTS.md`.
- Keep the diff on-topic. A refactor smuggled into a bug-fix phase is a
  review BLOCKER.
- Do not update README or ROADMAP to claim this works. Update them only when
  the gate is green and you have run the examples yourself.

## If you are blocked

Do not fake progress. Write what you tried, the exact error, and what you
believe is required into `FINDINGS.md`, then stop.

A blocked phase with an honest report is worth more than a green phase with a
lie in it. `verify.sh` will reject the phase anyway; a fabrication only adds a
blocking review finding on top.
